title: Max Depth (Textable, Numeric)
documentation:
## Purpose
Limits how many levels deep a machine traverses when extracting or generating a document outline or hierarchical structure.

## When to use
Set this parameter on outline extraction, table-of-contents generation, or tree-traversal machines to control output granularity. A depth of 1 returns only top-level headings; higher values include nested subsections.

## Notes
Valid range: 1–10. A depth of 1 is the shallowest (top-level only). Deep outlines may be large; balance depth against the token budget of downstream machines. See [Inspection Depth](https://capdag.com/browse/media:inspection-depth;textable) for a qualitative depth control.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
